rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order makes the denunciation of assigning partners to God general; placing jinn first would restrict the partnership to jinn.
rows.anchor: ويكون الجن في كلام ثان مقدر كأنه قيل فمن جعلوا شركاء قيل الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لما introduces a temporal condition; its answer may be an explicit nominal clause with fa, a negated clause, or an إذا-fajʾiyya clause.
rows.anchor: واما جوابها فقد يجئ ظاهرا كما ذكرنا قد يكون جملة اسمية مقرونة بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present-tense verb may answer لما while conveying past meaning, as in Abraham's disputing after the fear left him.
rows.anchor: وهو بمعنى الماضي أي جادلنا

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: The author prefers مقتصد itself as لما's answer over supplying an omitted division; he notes an objection that a clause with fa needs evidence.
rows.anchor: هو الذي ذكره ابن مالك ونوزع في ذلك من جهة إن خبرها مقرون بالفاء يحتاج لدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The جواب may be omitted; in Lot's لو أن لي بكم قوة, the implied answer is that he would have stopped them.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ لو أن لي بكم قوة ﴾ 6 جوابه محذوف أي لمنعتكم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One analysis makes the second لما the answer to the first, but the author objects to the answer's conjunction with fa.
rows.anchor: قيل جواب لما الأولى لما الثانية وجوابها ورد باقترانه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another analysis takes كفروا به as the answer to both instances, since the second لما repeats the first.
rows.anchor: وقيل ﴿ كفروا به ﴾ جواب لهما لان الثانية تكرير للاولى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A third analysis supplies an omitted answer to the first لما: they rejected it.
rows.anchor: وقيل جواب الاولى محذوف أي انكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For فلما أضاءت ما حوله, one view makes ذهب الله the answer; another omits the answer for brevity and lack of ambiguity.
rows.anchor: فقيل الجواب ﴿ ذهب الله ﴾ وقيل محذوف استطالة للكلام مع امن اللبس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The answer may be وأوحينا إليه if the conjunction waw is treated as extra.
rows.anchor: قيل الجواب قوله ﴿ وأوحينا إليه ﴾ 1 على جعل الواو زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb may substitute for a semantically corresponding verb and add clarification, as يضاعف explains يلق أثاما.
rows.anchor: ويبدل الفعل من الفعل الموافق له في المعنى مع زيادة بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون is a semantic apposition to the preceding destruction; apposition need not retain the original interrogative form.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت لو كان بدلا لكان معه الاستفهام قيل هو بدل معنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated apposition is illustrated: إذ هما في الغار apposes to إذ أخرجه, and إذ يقول لصاحبه to إذ هما.
rows.anchor: فقوله ﴿ إذ هما ﴾ بدل من قوله ﴿ إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ﴾ وقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آزر can clarify أب by preventing a figurative reading of father as grandfather, since Abraham calls earlier patriarchs his fathers.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن الأب يطلق على الجد بدليل قوله ﴿ آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam objects that apposition clarifies, while father is not ambiguous enough to need clarification.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عبد السلام والبدل لا يكون إلا للبيان والأب لايلتبس بغيزة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj, as quoted by al-Jawaliqi, says Abraham's father's name was Tarakh, while the Qur'an indicates Azar.
rows.anchor: في المعرب للجواليقي عن الزجاج لاخلاف ان اسم أبي إبراهيم تارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes Azar as an insult meaning ‘you err,’ a foreign word coinciding with Arabic; on this analysis the nominative reading is preferable.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالوجه الرفع في قراءة ﴿ آزر ﴾

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf requires البيان to be clearer than its head; the author rejects that condition, requiring only added clarity from their combination.
rows.anchor: وهو كالنعت في الايضاح وإزالة الإشتراك الكائن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The count of the opening letters signals that the Prophet had not practiced writing or learned its craft, as the verse says.
rows.anchor: التنبيه على أن تعداد هذه الحروف ممن لم يمارس الخط ولم يعان الطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourteen opening letters are half the alphabet if it has twenty-eight letters; the author instead holds that there are twenty-nine and لا has two letters.
rows.anchor: انحصارها فى نصف اسماء حروف المعجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alphabet's initial name alif is the name of hamza: alif itself cannot begin with a vowel, so lam provides its spoken name and its written form resembles alif.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت فقد تقدم اسم الألف فى أول حروف الهجاء قلت ذلك اسم الهمزة لوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a letter cannot be divided in half, one letter is necessarily omitted, with omission chosen as the more concise course.
rows.anchor: المذهب أن الحرف لا يمكن تنصيفه فيتعين سقوط حرف لأنه الأليق بالإيجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjoint letters occur in twenty-nine surahs, matching the alphabet's twenty-nine letters; their shapes were not matched because some are heavy to pronounce.
rows.anchor: مجيئها فى تسع وعشرين سورة بعدد الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orthographic convention writes alif as waw in four core words and four derivative forms, reflecting emphatic pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وذلك فى أربعة أصول مطردة وأربعة أحرف متفرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakat are Islam's pillars, life is the soul's basis and key to survival, and avoiding riba is a basis of security and a key to piety.
rows.anchor: فإن الصلاة والزكاة عمودا الإسلام والحياة قاعدة النفس ومفتاح البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riba contains forbidden and corrupt forms, opposes zakat, and avoiding it is foundational to financial conduct; the Qur'an pairs its erasure with the growth of charities.
rows.anchor: ويشتمل على أنواع الحرام وأنواع الخبائث وضروب المفاسد وهو نقيض الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riba is written with alif here because the verse does not refer to the universal category prohibited by God; negating a universal negates all its instances.
rows.anchor: فى سورة الروم لأنه ليس العام الكلى لأن الكلى منفى فى حكم الله عليه بالتحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is written with waw because the verse intends the universal category in God's judgment, as shown by the promise of multiplied reward.
rows.anchor: قلت لأن المراد بها الكلية فى حكم الله ولذلك قال ﴿ فأولئك هم المضعفون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining forms are meaningful too: salvation grounds obedience and happiness, morning begins human activity, the niche grounds guidance, and Manat represents misguidance and idolatry.
rows.anchor: وأما الغدوة فقاعدة الأزمان ومبدأ تصرف الإنسان

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi parses عليكم as an accusative exhortation; the majority reject this assumed construction.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي انتصب بعليكم على الاغراء وقدم المنصوب والجمهور على منع التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صبغة الله may confirm that believing as the believers did is God's religion, or it may be accusative as an imperative.
rows.anchor: لان هذا دين الله وقيل منصوبه على الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زلفى is a cognate accusative for an implied verb meaning ‘bring near’; منا and فداء similarly follow omitted verbs meaning ‘show favor’ and ‘ransom.’
rows.anchor: منصوبة على المصدر بما دل عليه الكلام

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh analyzes خلقه as an emphatic cognate accusative: God made each thing a good creation; alternatively, it may be an apposition of inclusion, ‘the creation of everything.’
rows.anchor: وجعل سيبويه من المصدر المؤكد لنفسه

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar prefers Sibawayh's analysis because it more emphatically expresses favor: each created thing is good and properly placed, not merely made well as an attempt.
rows.anchor: قال الصفار والذي قاله سيبويه اولى الامرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ on whether a cognate accusative or the verb is preferable for emphasis: the noun is lighter, while the verb can suggest continuity.
rows.anchor: هل الاولى التاكيد بالمصدر أو الفعل قال بعضهم المصدر اولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cognate accusative naming an action's kind normally takes a descriptive adjective; an adjective can also be supplied by an annexed phrase.
rows.anchor: حيث اكد المصدر النوعي فالاصل فيه ان ينعت بالوصف المراد منه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the repeated warning lets each report admonish listeners in its own right and keeps them from ease and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري 4 كرر ليجدوا عند سماع كل نبإ منها

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: In response to a skeptic, al-Hasan ibn Ali explained the denials against the claim that the parties would worship one another's gods in alternating months.
rows.anchor: يحكى أن بعض الزنادقة سأل الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنه عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is not redundant: it denies worship across past, present, and future; the past denial for both sides is omitted because the other two denials imply it.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن القصد نفى عبادته لآلهتهم في الآزمنة الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verbal negation denies that an act can occur, while a nominal negation denies being characterized by it; using both is stronger, as in the Prophet's inability to make the dead hear.
rows.anchor: وفيه تقدير آخر وهو أن الجملة الأولى فعلية والثانية أسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense denial indicates continuity, while the past form denies worship of their gods even once, completing the Prophet's lasting disavowal.
rows.anchor: فإن المضارع يدل على الدوام بخلاف الماضي فأفاد ذلك أن ما عبدتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parsing anomalous readings is often more technically demanding than parsing famous readings; al-Muhtasib is useful but incomplete, while al-Ukbari's work is broader.
rows.anchor: وتوجيه القراءة الشاذة أقوى في الصناعة من توجيه المشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the anomalous passive reading of أتخذ, the pronoun in وهو refers to وليا, resolving the apparent difficulty.
rows.anchor: على بناء الفعل الأول للمفعول دون الثانى وتأويل الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anomalous passive participle المُصوَّر is construed as the object of البارئ, which works like a verb: ‘the one who created the formed one.’
rows.anchor: بفتح الواو والراء على أنه اسم مفعول وتأويله أنه مفعول لاسم الفاعل

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anomalous reading is defensible if خشية here means reverential awe and glorification rather than fear.
rows.anchor: وتأويله أن الخشية هنا بمعنى الإجلال والتعظيم لا الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the tāʾ of عزمت read in the first person, the meaning is ‘when I guide and direct you’; على الله shifts the address, and attributing resolve to God is figurative.
rows.anchor: بضم التاء على التكلم لله تعالى وتأويله على معنى فإذا أرشدتك إليه

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Words that seem synonymous fit different contexts; khashya is stronger than khawf, which signals deficiency rather than total loss, so interpretation should preserve contextual distinctions.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك الخوف والخشية لايكاد اللغوي يفرق بينهما

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashya arises from the greatness of the one feared even when the fearer is strong; khawf arises from the fearer's weakness even when the danger is slight.
rows.anchor: بان الخشية تكون من عظم المخشى وان كان الخاشي قويا والخوف يكون من ضعف الخائف

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast ‘they revere their Lord and fear the bad reckoning’ reflects God's greatness; one who understands accounting and examines himself may not fear the reckoning.
rows.anchor: فان الخوف من الله لعظمته يخشاه كل أحد كيف كانت حالة

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse assigns khashya to scholars because knowledge makes God's greatness known.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى ﴿ إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's instruction to Moses not to fear addresses weakness in Moses, rather than diminishing the greatness of the threat.
rows.anchor: أي لايكون عندك من ضعف نفسك ما تخاف منه من فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that angels are said to fear their Lord is answered by their weakness relative to God, despite their strength among creatures.
rows.anchor: قيل الخاشي من الله بالنسبة إلى عظمه الله ضعيف

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For powerful angels, ‘fear’ makes their weakness before God explicit; for weak human believers, ‘revere’ points to God's greatness. ‘Above them’ means greatness, not place.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر المؤمنين من الناس وهم ضعفاء لاحاجة إلى بيان ضعفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn may precede humans because they are stronger and larger-bodied; the source cites the address to jinn and humans and Solomon's assembled forces.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهم أقوى أجساما وأعظم أقداما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration precedes bowing in one example of marked ordering; the source says an additional explanation was given earlier.
rows.anchor: ومنه تقديم السجد على الراكعين في قوله ﴿ واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse orders horses, mules, and donkeys in that sequence.
rows.anchor: ومنه تقديم الخيل على البغال والبغال على الحمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gold precedes silver; the author rejects an explanation based on masculine-before-feminine ordering because gold is feminine too, as ذهيبة shows.
rows.anchor: ومنه تقديم الذهب على الفضة

rows.speaker: الصوفية
rows.claim: Some Sufis cite wool's precedence to prefer wool garments and call wool the angels' clothing; reports from Ali, Abu Nuʿaym, and Ibn Masʿud praise wool, while a sound report says Moses wore a cloak.
rows.anchor: ولهذا احتج به بعض الصوفية على اختيار لبس الصوف على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is usually mentioned before the moon because it shines while the moon gives reflected light; a poet likewise says the moon draws its light from the sun.
rows.anchor: والحكماء يقولون إن نور القمر مستمد من نور الشمس

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: For the verse that mentions the moon before the sun, possible explanations are the verse endings or greater benefit to heaven's inhabitants; Ibn al-Anbari says the moon's face lights the sun's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل وجهين مناسبة رءوس الآي أو أن انتفاع أهل السموات به أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Word order can favor ease of pronunciation: Rabiʿa precedes the nobler Mudar to avoid consecutive vowels, and humans may precede jinn because ins is lighter to say.
rows.anchor: خفة اللفظ كما في قولهم ربيعة ومضر مع أن مضر أشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Form II can rarely indicate abundance with intransitive verbs, but in settings where abundance is impossible it does not carry that force.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء التضعيف دالا على الكثرة في اللازم قليلا نحو موت المال وجاء حيث لا يمكن فيه التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فأمتعه قليلا does not contradict an intensive reading: the enjoyment is called little because it ultimately runs out, diminishes, and perishes.
rows.anchor: وصفت بالقلة من حيث صيرورته إلى نفاد ونقص وفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Added intensity applies when a triliteral is transferred to an unlexicalized quadriliteral form; كلم موسى تكليما is not such a transfer and does not mean repeated speaking.
rows.anchor: لأنه غير منقول عن ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ترتيلا conveys abundant reading in a measured, reflective manner, whereas وما علمناه الشعر denies the basic act of teaching poetry rather than intensifying its negation.
rows.anchor: يدل على كثرة القراءة على هيئة التأني والتدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping after يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم is complete but not maximally complete, because the next verse gives its reason in meaning although not in syntax.
rows.anchor: فإن الوقف عليه تام ولكنه ليس بالأتم لأن ما بعده وهو قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stop need not wait until the end of a narrative; accordingly, some classify the stop after عليكم in the cited passage as incomplete.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم أتى به من جعل الوقف على ﴿ عليكم ﴾ من قوله

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi distinguishes حتى, which marks a definite endpoint, from إلى, which can mark any endpoint; eating a fish حتى its head works, but حتى half of it does not.
rows.anchor: وقال الكواشي في تفسيره الفرق بينهما إن حتى تختص بالغاية المضروبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a conjunction, حتى marks an endpoint of honor or lowliness, or the last state in a narrated situation; a prospective clause instead takes the subjunctive.
rows.anchor: ثم الغاية تجئ عاطفة وهي للغاية كيف وقعت اما في الشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a severe situation, حتى can introduce the final narrated state; if the clause is future, the following verb must be subjunctive.
rows.anchor: اما في الشدة نحو ﴿ وزلزلوا حتى يقول ﴾ 1 اذا اريد حكاية الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى marks the endpoint in phrases about the night and the completion of a term; in a comfortable state, it can introduce the last narrated state.
rows.anchor: ولانتهاء الغاية نحو ﴿ حتى مطلع الفجر ﴾ 1 ﴿ حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله ﴾ 2

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى can express purpose, where it can be replaced by كي; some examples about fighting or dispersal can also be read as endpoint.
rows.anchor: والتعليل وعلامتها إن تحسن في موضعها كي نحو حتى تغيظ ذا الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although حتى has been taken as exceptive in this phrase, the author says its apparent sense is endpoint.
rows.anchor: قيل وللاستثناء كقوله تعالى ﴿ وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا ﴾ 7 والظاهر انها للغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى may begin a nominal or verbal sentence; the response after حتى إذا is omitted in such constructions.
rows.anchor: وحرف ابتداء اي تبتدأ به الجملة الاسمية أو الفعلية

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows حيث as a time adverb as well as a place adverb; al-Zajjaj says its following clause is connective, not an annexed complement, which al-Farisi read as a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: حيث ظرف مكان قال الاخفش وللزمان وهي مبنية على الضم

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari objects that substitution is the strongest parsing for an exception after negation, though accusative is allowed; its use in both verses suggests a positive construction, answered by the author's point that negation is implicit.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشجري هذا يخالف أصح الإعرابين لأن المستثنى بعد النفي يقوى فيه البدل

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris explains لولا here as ‘they took gods besides God and do not bring authority for them.’
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن فارس منه ﴿ لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان ﴾ المعنى اتخذوا من دون الله آلهة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Ibn Barjan quotes al-Khalil that Qur'anic لولا means هلا except in Jonah's case, where its answer differs; the author questions this exception.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن برجان في تفسيره في أواخر سورة هود عن الخليل إن جميع ما في القرآن من لولا

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris treats لوما as close to لولا and explains it as هلا.
rows.anchor: هي قريب من لولا كقوله تعالى ﴿ لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة ﴾ 3 قال ابن فارس هي بمعنى هلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم governs a jussive imperfect while giving it past meaning; some Arabs use it with subjunctive, explaining the fatha in a reading of ألم نشرح through an underlying deleted light nūn of emphasis.
rows.anchor: لم نفي للمضارع وقبله ماضيا وتجزمه نحو ﴿ لم يلد ولم يولد ﴾

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The first لما enters an imperfect, makes it jussive, and gives it past sense; unlike لم, it negates an expected completed act and is stronger, since it combines لم with the opposite of قد.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري في الفائق لما مركبة من لم وما هي نقيضة قد

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abu al-Fath says adding ما to لم changes both meaning and form: it can mark the time when an event occurred and can be paused before its governed verb.
rows.anchor: وهذا اخذه من أبي الفتح فانه قال اصل لما لم زيدت عليها ما فصارت نفيا
